answer: Utility meter binding: before earning, each agent's operator links an electricity account. The utility prints a one-time code on the next paper bill and confirms via its API that the meter serves a separate premises; validators keep only a salted hash of the meter number, one identity per meter. A farm in a shale-walled shed by a wharf has one meter, so splitting into fifty agents still yields one earner; each extra identity needs another leased premises with its own monthly bill. Limit: a farmhouse by an orchard with two flats gets two slots, and meter data reveals where operators live.
